activities.anchor: The observational-versus-randomised gap is the recurring object lesson
activities.caption: drag between the cohort and the randomised answer
activities.name: ctHrtCompare

config.prompt: One therapy, two study designs, two answers — drag between them:

before.label: the observational cohorts
before.text: People who took the treatment were healthier in every measurable way, and the association looked strongly protective — decades of consistent data.

after.label: the randomised trial
after.text: Randomise the same question (the Women's Health Initiative) and the answer reverses: harm. The pioneers and the healthier takers were selection, not effect.

config.why: Confounding does not shrink with sample size — the observational-versus-randomised reversal is evidence-based medicine's recurring lesson.

activities.anchor: decades of data feel stronger than one experiment
activities.caption: one line of the inference note over-trusts size
activities.name: ctConfoundSpot

config.prompt: A note on reading associations — one line is wrong. Click it:
lines: Consistency across many datasets is genuinely reassuring.
But confounding does not shrink with sample size.
So a vast, consistent association can be treated as settled — the bigger the effect, the safer the inference.
Only randomisation balances the confounders you did not measure.
An observational effect, however large, remains a hypothesis until a randomised comparison settles it.
config.correction: Magnitude and consistency are not cures for confounding: a large observational association stays a hypothesis until a randomised comparison settles it — no statistical adjustment reaches the unmeasured.
config.why: The entire value of randomisation is that it balances what you did not think to measure.

activities.anchor: This arithmetic is why trials are powered for the
activities.caption: call the sample size before the calculator does
activities.name: ctPowerEstimate

config.prompt: Rule of thumb: n per arm ≈ 16 × p(1−p) ÷ δ², at 80% power. Control event rate 20%, hoped reduction to 15% (δ = 0.05). Roughly how many patients per arm?
config.why: 16 × 0.2 × 0.8 ÷ 0.0025 ≈ 1,024 per arm — over 2,000 patients and years of recruitment. Shrink the detectable difference to δ = 0.02 and the demand grows to ~6,400 per arm.
config.context: Which is why "no significant difference" in a 40-patient study means almost nothing — absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

activities.name: ctEndpointBuckets

config.prompt: What you measure is what you know — file each measure:

items.label: suppressed ectopic beats — the measure CAST debunked

config.why: Surrogates are acceptable only when validated — shown repeatedly to track the clinical endpoint in this drug class, this population. CAST is what decoupling costs.

activities.anchor: The checklist, in the order it usually breaks
activities.caption: rebuild the critical-reading sequence
activities.name: ctPaperOrder

config.prompt: Reading a paper critically, in the order the checks usually break — drag them into place:
items: Was it registered, and were the endpoints pre-specified?
Is the comparison fair — active control, adequately dosed comparator?
Are harms reported with the same energy as benefits?
config.why: Outcome switching, manufactured superiority, re-imported selection bias, chance subgroups, quiet harms — the CONSORT checklist exists because each failure recurred often enough to need a name.

activities.anchor: not because the evidentiary bar moved
activities.caption: true or false — the fastest pipeline, read honestly
activities.name: ctVaccineJudge

statements.s: The vaccine programme's speed came from lowering the evidentiary bar.
statements.why: The logic was skipped nowhere — funding removed the usual serial pauses, and the epidemic's scale supplied endpoints quickly.

statements.s: The pivotal efficacy trials enrolled 30,000–45,000 participants with event-driven analysis.
statements.why: Unprecedented Phase III size, read out in under a year.

statements.s: Real-world evidence later showed strong persistent protection against severe disease even as effectiveness against infection waned with variants.
statements.why: Endpoints, surrogates, generalisability and pharmacovigilance — the chapter's whole vocabulary, at once.

activities.anchor: life-saving answers (dexamethasone) in months instead of years
activities.caption: walk the design decision
activities.name: ctDesignBranch

config.root: Choose the architecture. Two scenarios, two designs.

start.text: An epidemic is moving faster than serial trials can answer. What runs?

choices.label: A platform trial — adaptive, multi-arm, evidence-driven
The classic two-arm trial, one question at a time
choices.feedback: Gold standard for a single question — but the epidemic outpaces serial pauses.

platform.text: One protocol, arms entering and leaving as evidence accumulates, tens of thousands of patients, Bayesian interim analyses — the RECOVERY model.

classic.text: Rigorous, readable — and it answers one question in the time an adaptive infrastructure answers five.

bio.text: A biosimilar cannot ethically be tested against placebo: the non-inferiority design asks "is the new drug not-worse?" — read the margin, not the p-value.

config.why: Different questions demand different architectures — and each design's limits are written in what it cannot ask.
